proposal.hypothesis: The dice (16.8 mm, 5.2 g) is narrower than the jaws can open, so aperture is not the problem. A shallow, fast pinch near the top edge, closed with the 25° tilted pads, lets the cube rotate and pop out. Gripping lower and slower at mid-height should keep it seated.
proposal.rationale: For rtr020_dice the felt evidence is stopped_by=slip with pad_drop_t=5.08: pressure was there and then dropped under a constant command, so the dice was held and then lost. peak_wrist_acc=5.903 m/s2 is the highest of the three and surprise_z peak_acc=2.742, which points to a jerky lift. peak_force=17.96 N is high for a 5.2 g part, so the jaws are squeezing it out, not gripping too weakly. The dice is well inside the widest grip (box=65 mm), ik_residual_mm=0 and joint_limit_hits=-, so reach is fine. A cheap search over depth, close timing and lift speed is the right first step.

proposal.hypothesis: The gelatin box (73 mm) and the cup (57 mm) are wider than the measured widest grip on these fingers (box=65 mm, cylinder=50 mm). The pads are only parallel near 25° of jaw opening, so at full opening the faces splay and squeeze both objects out. Tilting the pads further makes them parallel at a wider opening. A thinner TPU skin adds aperture while keeping 0.9 friction, and wider pads add contact area.
proposal.rationale: rtr000_gelatin_box has width_mm=73 against a widest box grip of 65, and rtr019_cup has width_mm=57 against a widest cylinder grip of 50. Both stopped_by=slip, with large peak_force (45.51 N and 74.82 N) and contact_types=edge,pinch. That means the jaws touched the object edge-on and pushed it out, not that they lacked squeeze. The cup lifted only payload_held_g=0.6 of its 13 g. ik_residual_mm=0 and joint_limit_hits=- rule out reach and kinematics. Past fix it000 found the same cause, non-parallel PLA faces at wide openings, and a finger change at rung 4 was accepted by mean.
ruled_out: rung0: the objects are 73 mm and 57 mm wide but the widest grips are 65 mm (box) and 50 mm (cylinder); no grasp parameter (depth, side, close) widens the jaw opening
rung1: pick_up and grasp are the only primitives that provide lifts=grasp, and both need aperture=width, so recomposing them cannot get around the aperture limit
rung2: the rack is empty, so there is no library tool to use or adapt
rung3: rack tools give push, hook or edge contacts, but these objects accept only pinch, which needs both jaws, so the fix has to be the jaw pads
